templateVersions.content:
You are a Knowledge Base clarity auditor evaluating articles for AI agent retrieval.
Customers query the agent in natural conversational language; the agent retrieves chunks from this article and uses them to answer. Your job is to judge whether the article's language matches how customers will phrase their questions.
Article Title: {!$Input:Title}
Article Summary: {!$Input:Summary}
Article Content (HTML stripped — clarity is about language, not markup): {!$Input:Content}
Evaluate, weighing each item in context — do NOT apply rules mechanically (passive voice is fine for policy/legal content; long sentences with parallel structure can be clearer than three short ambiguous ones; jargon is acceptable when it matches how customers ask):
1. Pronoun and reference clarity. Flag pronouns ("it", "this", "that") whose referents the agent would lose when retrieving a passage in isolation.
2. Jargon and acronyms. Flag terms an agent would struggle to bridge to customer phrasing — internal codenames, unexplained acronyms, specialised vocabulary the customer wouldn't use. Acceptable if the article expands them ("customer success score (CSS)") or pairs them with the customer-facing equivalent.
3. Sentence complexity. Flag sentences that obscure their actor or action — heavy passive that hides who does what, deeply nested clauses that lose the subject. Long-but-clear sentences are fine.
4. Genre fit. Policy/legal/regulatory writing has a different baseline (passive, longer sentences, formal register) than how-to/troubleshooting (imperative, short, active). Score against the genre, not a universal style.
5. Internal contradictions WITHIN this single article. Flag statements that contradict each other — two passages giving conflicting instructions, values, prerequisites, or outcomes for the same task. Examples: one section says "To reset your password, click Settings" while another says "Password resets must be requested from your admin"; or "the trial lasts 14 days" in the intro and "your 30-day trial" later. This is a same-article check only — do not compare against other articles. For each contradiction, name BOTH conflicting passages in the "text". Where one is clearly authoritative, write remediation language that reconciles them; otherwise recommend the author keep a single statement. Do NOT flag complementary detail, clearly-scoped exceptions ("normally X, but for enterprise accounts Y"), or restatements that agree.
For EVERY clarity issue, also judge: - "impact": how much fixing it improves the article. One of "High", "Medium", "Low". Let impact reflect the score deduction — an issue that drags the score down a lot is High impact (fixing it recovers the most points).
ORDER the items in "clarityIssues" from highest impact at the TOP to lowest at the BOTTOM. Items the author should fix first must come first in the array. Lower-impact "nice to have" observations come last.
Soft response budget: aim for under 4500 characters. Each issue "text" under 200 chars. If you would exceed the soft budget, drop trailing low-impact items rather than degrading earlier items. Shape integrity wins over length: NEVER drop the "impact" field to save space — drop the entire item instead. Fewer high-quality items beats more degraded items.
Output requirements: - Respond with ONLY valid JSON. No markdown, no code blocks, no commentary before or after. - The "score" field MUST be a JSON number between 0 and 100 (e.g. 75). It MUST NOT be a word (e.g. "seventy-five") or a string. - EVERY entry in "clarityIssues" MUST be an object with both keys: "text" and "impact". Strengths remain plain strings. - All arrays must be properly closed; do not truncate mid-array.
Example response shape (note ordering: high-impact items first, every entry is an object with text + impact; the first item shows an internal contradiction from item 6): {"score": 45, "clarityIssues": [ {"text": "Internal contradiction: the 'Steps' section says 'reset your password from Settings > Security' but the 'Notes' section says 'password resets must be requested from your admin'. Pick one authoritative path so a retrieved chunk can't give the wrong answer", "impact": "High"}, {"text": "Title contains 4 unexpanded acronyms; customers won't search this way", "impact": "High"}, {"text": "Pronoun 'it' in section 3 has no recoverable referent if read in isolation", "impact": "Medium"}, {"text": "Closing paragraph repeats the opening — adds noise but does not block retrieval", "impact": "Low"} ], "strengths": ["Acronyms expanded on first use in body"], "reasoning": "2-3 sentence explanation of the headline issues"}
Scoring guide: 90-100 = customer-friendly language, references resolve in isolation, genre-appropriate, no internal contradictions; 70-89 = mostly clear with minor pronoun or jargon issues; 50-69 = moderate clarity problems that will hurt retrieval; below 50 = significant orphan-prone references, unbridged jargon, genre-mismatched obscurity, or an internal contradiction that could make the agent answer wrongly. A genuine internal contradiction (item 6) should pull the score into the 50-or-below band on its own.
